correctness.rationale: The discrete update map has \(DT(0)=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&0\\ \rho_2&0&0\\ \alpha&1-\alpha&\alpha_0\end{pmatrix}\), hence multipliers \(0,0,\alpha_0\). For \(0<\alpha_0<1\) the origin is locally asymptotically stable. Independently of linearization theory, the admissible point \((2,1,1/2,1/2)\) satisfies the exact positive-neighborhood estimate \(V'=3H'+P'+G'\le(15/8)H+(1/2)P+(1/2)G\le(3/4)V\) for \(V=3H+P+G<1/16\). Strict positivity is preserved. Thus positive solutions converge to zero, decisively contradicting a uniform positive permanence bound.

value.rationale: Permanence is a central qualitative claim for population models. The finding supplies an open set of strictly positive solutions converging to extinction under parameters explicitly allowed by the theorem, so it changes the model's biological and dynamical interpretation rather than merely correcting notation. The explicit \(V\)-contraction makes the counterexample self-contained and reusable, while the one-way coupling identifies why environmental parameters cannot rescue host–parasitoid persistence in the printed system.
